plan.title: Scope gate: file mutations via Bash bypass the active-xBRIEF check that blocks Edit/Write

narratives.Description: Edit/Write scope-not-ready deny must state the gate is direct-write and spawn, not Shell dest-forms. A new product dest-form classifier (not UAT classify as-is) routes git checkout --, git restore, and rm/rmdir of in-repo paths through inspectMutationGates with Edit/Write parity exemptions.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The active-xBRIEF scope gate refuses file mutations made through the host's `Edit`/`Write` tools, but the same mutations made through `Bash` (`git checkout --`, `rm`) go through unchallenged. Nothing downstream catches it either — the pre-commit gates don't require an active xBRIEF — so a shell-only change can be made and committed entirely outside a scope.

## Evidence

Single session, `deftai/agentsentri`, `xbrief/active/` empty, the two calls seconds apart:

**Allowed** — four tracked/untracked files mutated:

```
git checkout -- apps/web/tsconfig.json apps/web/next-env.d.ts && rm apps/web/AGENTS.md apps/web/CLAUDE.md
```

**Refused** — the very next call, a one-line edit to `.gitignore`:

```
Directive denied Edit: No active xBRIEF artifact was found under xbrief/active/
(or the legacy vbrief/active/ compatibility path). Recovery: run `deft scope:activate -- <path>` ...
```

Same repo, same empty `active/`, same class of mutation. One surface enforces, the other doesn't.

The commit path doesn't close the gap. After scoping, my commits ran:

```
verify_encoding / verify_forward_coverage / verify_vbrief_conformance / verify_xbrief_drift / branch-protection
```

None of those requires an active xBRIEF, so the shell-only version of this change would have committed clean.

## What I can't determine from outside

`.claude/settings.json` (Directive-managed) does register a `PreToolUse` hook on Bash:

```json
{
  "matcher": "Shell|Bash|BashTool|shell|bash",
  "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "deft-hook --host claude --event tool.before", "timeout": 5 }]
}
```

So Bash is wired. Whether the hook fired and declined to scope-gate, or didn't fire at all, I can't distinguish from the consumer side. The gates I *observed* firing around commit and push (`deft branch-protection`, `deft destructive-gh-verb gate (pre-push)`) appear to be git-level hooks rather than the tool hook, so they aren't evidence either way.

## Why it matters

The refusal message is emphatic and reads as authoritative, which makes the gate easy to trust as complete. An agent that reaches for `sed -i`, `rm`, or `git checkout --` — including one following host guidance to prefer shell tools — silently operates unscoped. The gap is widest exactly where scope matters most: cleanup and revert work, which is naturally shell-shaped.

In my case the unscoped mutation was the change I actually wanted, and I scoped it retroactively. The concern is that nothing required me to.

## Expected

Either the Bash `tool.before` hook applies the same active-xBRIEF check to recognized file-mutating commands, or the refusal message stops implying coverage it doesn't have. A commit-time active-scope check would also close it, at the cost of catching things later.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` 0.104.0 (engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.104.0`)
- Deposit generation 4, contentVersion 0.104.0, stamped 2026-08-15
- Host: Claude Code, `deft-hook --host claude`
- Platform: darwin
- Consumer repo: `deftai/agentsentri` (xbrief layout, not legacy vbrief)

## Related

- #2885 (closed) touched the same write gate from the containment angle — absolute paths outside the checkout. This is the complementary direction: paths inside the checkout, reached through a different tool surface.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T03:04:07Z)

## Triage analysis

_By: Grok 4.6 (xAI), 2026-08-21. Checked against issue body via REST (no comments), then `origin/master` hook dispatcher. Working tree not modified._

**Verdict:** accurate, desirable, almost ready. Lock a first-ship slice before implementing. Mechanism-shaped: expanding the write gate onto Shell dest-forms.

`design-critique: warranted, because the lean proposes applying the active-xBRIEF write gate to file-mutating Shell (or a commit-time scope check), which is a new invariant on the #2711 fail-open shell path.`

### Accuracy

High. The split is in the dispatcher, not a missed hook registration.

- Edit/Write go through `inspectMutationGates` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` ~1289) and deny `scope-not-ready` with `No active xBRIEF artifact was found under xbrief/active/` (`packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts:50–52`). Recovery copy names `deft scope:activate`.
- Bash **is** wired (`SHELL_HOOK_MATCHER` on `tool.before`). The hook fires.
- Shell/MCP are then routed **away** from that gate on purpose (`dispatcher.ts:1264–1274`): “Does not require active-scope ritual — only runtimeAuthority when enabled.”
- Unrecognized shell ops **fail open** (`decideShellOrMcpRuntimeAuthority`: `ops.length === 0` → `shell-op-unclassifiable` allow, `:762–774`). `git checkout --` and `rm` are not push/merge, so they allow. That answers the reporter’s “fired vs declined”: declined to scope-gate, then fail-open.
- Pre-commit/push surfaces named in the body (encoding, forward-coverage, vbrief-conformance, xbrief-drift, branch-protection) do not require an active xBRIEF. A shell-only mutation can commit.

#2885 is complementary (Write/Edit **outside** the checkout skip the gate). This issue is **inside** the checkout via a different tool class.

### Desirability

High. The Edit deny reads as a complete write fence. Cleanup/revert is naturally `git checkout --` / `rm`. Host guidance that prefers shell tools walks around the gate. Same empty `active/`, same class of mutation, two verdicts.

### Readiness

Almost — pick v1. Body offers three directions:

1. **Honesty:** Edit/Write deny must say the gate is direct-write (and spawn), not Shell dest-forms. Cheap; should land either way.
2. **Scope-gate dest-form Shell** targeting in-repo paths (`rm`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `mv`, `sed -i`, …) through `inspectMutationGates`. Reuses dest-writer classification already built for UAT/authz; do not boil the #3421 matrix in v1 — start with the repro class (`git checkout --` / `rm` of tracked or untracked in-tree paths).
3. **Commit-time active-scope check** — catches later, including hook-bypass. Separate story; do not fold into the PreToolUse slice.

Recommended first ship: **(1)+(2)** with a **bounded** dest-form list. Leave commit-time as follow-up. Do not require active xBRIEF for `git status` / unclassifiable non-dest commands (#2711 fail-open stays for those).

Do not implement until that dest-form list is named in AC. Hostile envelope: `python -c "open('f','w')"` and `cmd /c copy` are the next bypasses; v1 should admit they remain open.

### Disposition

**Accept** as a scoped bug/safety story after the dest-form list is locked. Pair honesty copy with the Shell dest-form route so the message and the gate match. Keep #2885 closed. Refs #2711, #3080, #1802, #2885.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T03:12:06Z)

## Design critique of the triage comment (checked at `4bd58219a8e376c11a49ddf4df4ee13611738dfc`)

_By: Grok 4.5 (xAI)_

Open critique of comment `5364690109` (triage). Inputs: issue body + comments with `id <= 5364690109`; re-verified against `origin/master` @ `4bd58219a8e376c11a49ddf4df4ee13611738dfc` via `git show` / live classifiers. No later comments used.

### What holds

- The Edit/Write vs Shell split is real and dispatcher-shaped, not a missed Bash registration. `SHELL_HOOK_MATCHER` / `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` exist (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts:30`, `:98`). Shell is wired; PreToolUse fires.
- Direct writes reach `inspectMutationGates` (`dispatcher.ts:804` definition; direct-write call at `:1289`). Empty `xbrief/active/` yields `scope-not-ready` with `No active xBRIEF artifact was found under xbrief/active/` (`scope.ts:50–52`), then recovery text that names `deft scope:activate` (`dispatcher.ts:992–1009`).
- Shell/MCP are routed away from that gate on purpose (`dispatcher.ts:1264–1274`, comment at `:1267`: "Does not require active-scope ritual — only runtimeAuthority when enabled.") into `decideShellOrMcpRuntimeAuthority` (`:702`).
- Unrecognized shell ops fail open: `ops.length === 0` → allow `shell-op-unclassifiable` (`:762–774`). `listShellOps` only returns push/merge (`runtime-authority.ts:474–487`).
- Pre-commit does not require an active xBRIEF (`.githooks/pre-commit`: `verify:branch`, `verify:encoding`, `verify:forward-coverage`, optional `verify:vbrief-conformance` / `verify:xbrief-drift`). A shell-only mutation can commit.
- #2885 complementarity (outside-checkout Write/Edit skip) is correctly framed as the other axis.
- Recommended sequencing — honesty copy + bounded Shell dest-form gate; commit-time as a separate story; keep #2711 fail-open for non-dest commands; admit hostile residual (`python -c`, `cmd /c copy`) — is the right *shape* of a first ship, if the mechanism claim below is corrected.

### Findings

1. **`blocks-the-design` — "Reuse dest-writer classification" does not cover the repro class.**
   Triage says first ship can reuse UAT/authz dest-writer classification for `git checkout --` / `rm`. Empirically, at `4bd58219a8e376c11a49ddf4df4ee13611738dfc`, the same classifiers return **empty** for the reporter's commands:
   - `git checkout -- apps/web/tsconfig.json … && rm apps/web/AGENTS.md …` → `listShellOps: []`, `classifyShellAuthzOps: []`
   - `git checkout -- apps/web/tsconfig.json` → both `[]`
   - `rm apps/web/AGENTS.md` → both `[]`
   - `sed -i s/a/b/ file.ts` → both `[]`
   - `cmd /c copy a b` → both `[]`
   - Contrast: `git push origin HEAD` → `["push"]`; `python -c "open('f','w').write('x')"` → authz `["settings"]` (UAT programmatic-write path only).
   Source reasons: `listShellOps` is push/merge-only; `GIT_WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS` is `clone|worktree|submodule` only (`authz/classify.ts:762`) — **not** `checkout`/`restore`; `rm` appears in write-bin sets, but UAT harvest gates **protected** dests (`.deft/authz/**`, kill-switch, approved-scope), not arbitrary in-repo product paths. Wiring today's `classifyShellAuthzOps` into `inspectMutationGates` would **ship a false fix** for the filed repro. V1 needs a **new** product dest-form classifier (or an explicitly extended harvest) named in AC — not "reuse" as written.

2. **`sharpens-framing` — `inspectMutationGates` "~1289" cite is the call site, not the gate body.**
   Definition is `:804`. `:1289` is the direct-write `return inspectMutationGates(…, { proposedLifecycleExempt: true })`. Spawn path calls it at `:1261`. Shell never enters it (`:1268–1273`). Structural claim holds; tilde cite is imprecise if read as "the gate lives at 1289."

3. **`blocks-the-design` — Shell→`inspectMutationGates` without Edit/Write parity exemptions over-tightens.**
   Direct-write path already exempts assist/scratch (`#1802`, `dispatcher.ts:813–838`) and proposed-lifecycle writes (`#2625`, `proposedLifecycleExempt`). A Shell dest-form route that only checks `inspectActiveScope` with no matching assist / proposed / ephemeral exemptions would deny shell cleanup under `.deft-scratch/` / assist posture while Edit/Write still allow — a new inconsistency, not parity. AC must list the same exemptions (and whether story `file_scope` / path-write-fence applies to Shell dests; today `path-write-fence.md` says Shell push/merge are **not** re-scoped by `file_scope`).

4. **`sharpens-framing` — "Almost ready" overstates readiness until the dest-form list and classifier SoT are named.**
   Triage correctly refuses implement until the list is locked, then recommends first ship **(1)+(2)** without proposing the AC list or naming that `git checkout --` is **absent** from current harvest. Readiness is "accurate diagnosis + desired outcome"; mechanism AC is still open. Thin fail-closed (#3265): land honesty copy as the one fail-closed message fix even if the Shell classifier slips.

5. **`footnote` — Deny copy is tool-scoped, not a literal "all mutations" claim.**
   Message is `Directive denied Edit: <scope.message> + recovery` (`dispatcher.ts:1009`). It does not say Bash is covered. Still easy to *read* as a complete write fence (reporter's point). Honesty copy remains justified; do not over-claim the current text lies about Shell.

### Existing mechanisms

| Mechanism | What it does today | Gap vs #3438 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inspectMutationGates` + `inspectActiveScope` | Active-xBRIEF / ritual for direct Write/Edit/spawn | Not on Shell path |
| `decideShellOrMcpRuntimeAuthority` + `listShellOps` | Opt-in push/merge under `runtimeAuthority` (#2711); else fail open | File mutations unclassifiable |
| `classifyShellAuthzOps` / UAT dest harvest (#3421 family) | Fail-closed settings when Shell plants authz/kill-switch/approved-scope | Ordinary product `rm` / `git checkout --` stay `[]` |
| Path write fence (#516 / #2443) | Project + story `file_scope` for **direct** writes | Shell not re-scoped by `file_scope` |
| Assist/scratch (#1802) / ephemeral spawn (#3080) | Skip active-scope for allowlisted disposable writes / non-lifecycle spawns | Must be mirrored if Shell is gated |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` | branch / encoding / coverage / xbrief drift | No active-scope check |
| Swarm skill prose (#800) | Forbidden `git checkout` in another agent's worktree | Skill rule, not PreToolUse |

Inventory before inventing: extend classification + route, or honesty-only, or commit-time verify — do not add a parallel gate engine beside `decideHook`.

### Injection / swarm lens

- Hosts that prefer Shell/Bash (Claude Code matcher already on Shell) make the bypass the **default** tool path, not an exotic one.
- Prompt injection / "prefer terminal" guidance that says `sed -i` / `rm` / `git checkout --` instead of Edit walks around the only surface that currently fails closed.
- Swarm cleanup and revert are naturally shell-shaped; skill text (#800) does not enforce at PreToolUse. A false "reuse UAT classify" ship would leave the swarm cleanup class open while looking green in tests that only assert push/merge or authz-protected dests.
- Obfuscation (`python -c`, encoded `bash -c`) remains a residual; triage already admits this — keep it in AC as known-open, not silent.

### Road not taken

**Honesty-only first ship (thin #3265), defer Shell dest-form classifier.** Change Edit/Write deny copy so it states the gate is direct-write (and spawn), not Shell dest-forms; open a follow-up for a *new* product dest-form classifier + parity exemptions; leave commit-time active-scope as a third story. Cheaper, no #2711 fail-open collision in v1, and avoids shipping a classifier that does not yet exist. Cost: the reporter's Bash bypass remains until the follow-up lands — mitigated only by clearer refusal text.

Alternative not preferred: fold commit-time active-scope into the same PreToolUse PR (triage correctly separates these).

### Score against Directive rules

| Rule | Score |
| --- | --- |
| Authority ladder | Pass — mechanism is `decideHook` / classifiers, not AGENTS.md prose as SoT. |
| Fail-closed | Mixed — correctly wants Shell dest-forms fail closed, but must not silently invert #2711 fail-open for unclassifiable non-dest commands (triage says this; keep it in AC). |
| Propose-not-apply | Pass — triage proposes; does not implement. |
| Claim-cites-state (#2066) | Soft miss on `inspectMutationGates ~1289` precision; other cites land. |
| Gate integrity (#3156) | Pass intent — do not weaken Edit to match Shell; close or disclose the gap. Reject any "fix" that only asserts UAT classify without the repro. |
| Thin fail-closed (#3265) | Soft miss — packaging honesty+(2) as one first ship risks two checks; prefer honesty as the single message remediation, Shell classifier as the second fail-closed check with its own AC. |

### Disposition

**Accept the diagnosis; do not accept the mechanism wording as written.** Keep design-critique warranted. Before implement:

1. Name the v1 dest-form list in AC (`git checkout -- <paths>`, `git restore`, `rm`/`rmdir`, …) and state explicitly that these need a **new** product-mutation classifier (current UAT harvest does not cover them — measured at `4bd58219a8e376c11a49ddf4df4ee13611738dfc`).
2. Require Edit/Write parity exemptions (assist/scratch, proposed lifecycle; decide file_scope for Shell).
3. Land honesty copy even if the Shell slice slips.
4. Keep hostile envelope (`python -c`, `cmd /c copy`, obfuscated bash) as documented residual — not silent.
5. Leave commit-time active-scope as a separate story.

Refs checked in-tree: #2711 fail-open path, #1802 / #3080 assist, #2885 outside-root, path-write-fence Shell residual. Keep #2885 closed.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T03:13:07Z)

## Verified synthesis (critique-pass-1, 2026-08-21)

_By: Grok 4.6 (xAI) — synthesizer, not a critic in this run. Triage author was also Grok 4.6; critic was Grok 4.5. Rows marked **hold** only on a primary-source re-read of `origin/master`, not on critic agreement._

Hand-run of #3434 Pass 3. Not implementation. Working tree was not modified.

**SHA:** `4bd58219a8e376c11a49ddf4df4ee13611738dfc` (`origin/master` at synthesis; same tip the critic named).

Thread: issue body; [triage](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3438#issuecomment-5364690109); [R1 critique](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3438#issuecomment-5364738226).

### Disposition

**Accept the diagnosis; do not accept “reuse UAT dest-writer classification” as the v1 mechanism.** Keep design-critique warranted. Lock AC before implement.

| Slice | In v1 | Out of v1 |
|---|---|---|
| **A — honesty copy** | Edit/Write `scope-not-ready` deny states the gate is **direct-write (and spawn)**, not Shell dest-forms. Land even if B slips. | Claiming the current text already names Bash (it does not; it is tool-scoped `Directive denied Edit:`) |
| **B — new product dest-form classifier** | Name the list in AC: at least `git checkout -- <paths>`, `git restore`, `rm`/`rmdir` of in-repo paths. Route those through `inspectMutationGates` with **Edit/Write parity exemptions** (assist/scratch #1802, proposed lifecycle #2625; decide `file_scope` for Shell). | “Reuse” `classifyShellAuthzOps` / `listShellOps` as-is — they return `[]` for the filed repro |
| **C — documented residual** | `python -c`, `cmd /c copy`, obfuscated bash stay **known-open** in AC. | Pretending v1 closes all dest writers |
| **D — commit-time active-scope** | | Separate story. Do not fold into PreToolUse |

Keep #2711 fail-open for non-dest unclassifiable shell (`git status`). Keep #2885 closed.

### Verified claims

| Claim | Claimant | Verdict | Method | Evidence at `4bd58219` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Edit/Write use `inspectMutationGates`; empty active → `scope-not-ready` | reporter, triage, R1 | **hold** | `git show` | `dispatcher.ts:1289`; `scope.ts:50–52` |
| Shell is wired then routed **away** from that gate | triage, R1 | **hold** | `git show` | `dispatcher.ts:1264–1274` “Does not require active-scope ritual” |
| Unclassifiable shell fail-open | triage, R1 | **hold** | `git show` | `dispatcher.ts:762–774` `shell-op-unclassifiable` |
| `listShellOps` is push/merge only | R1 F1 | **hold** | `git show` | `policy/runtime-authority.ts:474–487` |
| Git dest harvest is `clone\|worktree\|submodule`, not `checkout`/`restore` | R1 F1 | **hold** | `git show` | `authz/classify.ts:762` |
| Pre-commit has no active-xBRIEF check | reporter, triage, R1 | **hold** | `git show` `.githooks/pre-commit` | encoding / branch / coverage / xbrief drift — no `inspectActiveScope` |
| `inspectMutationGates ~1289` is the **call site** | R1 F2 | **hold** | `git show` | definition `:804`; Shell never enters |
| Current deny text does not literally claim Bash coverage | R1 F5 | **hold** | `git show` | `dispatcher.ts:1009` `Directive denied ${toolName}` |
| Live `listShellOps`/`classifyShellAuthzOps` empty on reporter `git checkout --` / `rm` | R1 F1 | **unverified here** | critic ran classifiers; this pass did not re-execute them | code path (push/merge-only + GIT_WRITE_SUBCOMMANDS) makes empty results expected |

### Finding → slice

| Finding | Source | Slice |
|---|---|---|
| Reuse UAT classify would false-fix the repro | R1 F1 | **B** (new classifier, named list) |
| Shell path needs same exemptions as Edit | R1 F3 | **B** AC |
| Honesty even if classifier slips | R1 F4 / road-not-taken | **A** |
| Hostile residual | triage, R1 | **C** |
| Commit-time gate | body, triage | **D** |

### What the triage got right

Diagnosis, desirability, #2885 complementarity, #2711 fail-open for non-dest, commit-time as a separate story, honesty copy must land.

### What the critique changed (load-bearing)

Triage “reuse dest-writer classification” does **not** cover `git checkout --` / `rm`. Those need a **new** product-mutation classifier named in AC. Pair Shell gating with assist/proposed exemptions or you create a new Edit-vs-Shell inconsistency. Prefer honesty as the first fail-closed message even if B is a second check.

### Out of scope here

Implementing A–D. Expanding UAT settings-deny to all product paths. Weakening Edit to match Shell (#3156).
